problems.title: The correct exponential identity
problems.question: For f(x)=aˣ,a>0,which identity holds for every real α,β,x,y?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: a^(u+v)=aᵘaᵛ; (aˣ)^α=a^(αx).

problems.title: An exponential graph in three quadrants
problems.question: Which listed exponential passes through quadrants I,II,IV?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: For f(x)=2^(−x)−1/2,the zero is x=1.
steps: For all negative x,f(x)>0,so the left branch is in quadrant II.
For0<x<1 it is positive,quadrant I; for x>1 it is negative,quadrant IV.

problems.title: Volume and a normal prism section
problems.question: An oblique quadrilateral prism has volume48 and lateral edge6. Find the area of a section perpendicular to that edge.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Prism volume=normal-section area times lateral-edge length.

problems.title: A quadratic whose coefficients are logarithms
problems.question: Solve x²+2=log₂(3ˣ)+log₃(4ˣ).
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Let u=log₂3,v=log₃4. Then uv=2.

problems.title: Integer logarithm bases in a value interval
problems.question: How many integers x satisfy logₓ199∈[2,3]?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: The base must be x>0,x≠1. Integer bases are therefore x≥2.

problems.title: Change a logarithm base
problems.question: Given lg5=a,lg3=b,express log₃₀8.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: log₃₀8=lg8/lg30; lg2=1−a.

problems.title: A sphere inside a cone frustum
problems.question: A cone frustum contains a tangent sphere. Distances from its center to the two base circumferences are3 and4. Find the sum of base diameters.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: For frustum radii r,R and sphere radiusρ,the axial tangential trapezoid givesρ²=rR.
steps: Squared center-to-rim distances are r²+ρ²=9 and R²+ρ²=16.

problems.title: Equal axial-section and base areas
problems.question: A cone’s axial-section area equals its base area. Find the tangent of a generator’s angle to the base.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Axial triangle area=rh; base area=πr².

problems.title: An exponential equation with a monotone substitution
problems.question: Solve27ˣ+12ˣ=2·8ˣ.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Divide by8ˣ>0 and set t=(3/2)ˣ>0.
steps: t³+t−2=(t−1)(t²+t+2),whose quadratic factor is positive. Thus t=1.

problems.title: Which equation has only finitely many roots?
problems.question: Which listed equation does not have infinitely many real solutions?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: log₂x is strictly increasing on x>0,while0.3ˣ is strictly decreasing.
steps: Their difference is strictly increasing and changes from negative near0 to positive for large x,so exactly one intersection exists.
The trigonometric choices have crossings on infinitely many oscillations or tangent branches. The conjugate-exponential choice is an identity since(2+√3)(2−√3)=1.

problems.title: Circumsphere of a square pyramid
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has height and base diagonal both24. Find its circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Base circumradiusρ=12; R=(h²+ρ²)/(2h).

problems.title: A sphere through cube edge midpoints
problems.question: Find the radius of the sphere through all edge midpoints of a cube with edge√8.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: From the cube center to an edge midpoint,the coordinate offsets are a/2,a/2,0.

problems.title: A logarithmic equation becomes a cube
problems.question: Solve(lgx)²+lgx+1=7log_(x/10)10.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Let t=lgx,x>0,x≠10. Then log_(x/10)10=1/(t−1).
steps: Thus t=2 and x=10²,which is allowed.

problems.title: Product of two logarithmic roots
problems.question: Find the product of roots of[log₃(81x)]²+[log₃(27x)]²=5.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Set t=log₃x,so the equation is(t+4)²+(t+3)²=5.
steps: The x roots are3⁻²,3⁻⁵; multiply them.

problems.title: Factor a two-variable exponential relation
problems.question: Given2^(x+y+1)−2^(y+1)−2ˣ=−1,find x(y+1).
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Move1 to the left and factor:(2ˣ−1)(2^(y+1)−1)=0.

problems.title: Radius ratio for a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: Find circumsphere radius divided by insphere radius in a regular tetrahedron.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: The common center divides an altitude in ratio3:1 from the vertex.

problems.title: Fit two spheres into a cylinder
problems.question: A cylindrical box has base radius8. What minimum height holds two spheres of radius5?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Each sphere center lies within radius8−5=3 of the cylinder axis.
steps: Their greatest possible horizontal separation is6. Their centers must be at least10 apart,so vertical separation is at least√(100−36)=8.
There must also be5 clearance above the upper center and below the lower center. Minimum height=5+8+5.
Opposite horizontal center positions at radius3 achieve the bound.

problems.title: A real power defined for every real input
problems.question: Which listed expression defines a real-valued function for every real x?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: For x≠0,the base x² is positive; at x=0,the exponent1−x equals1.
steps: Thus(x²)^(1−x) is defined for all nonzero x and takes value0¹=0 at zero.
Other candidates involve a negative base to arbitrary real powers or0⁰ at zero.

problems.title: A system in two exponential variables
problems.question: Which listed pair solves4ˣ+9ʸ=74 and2ˣ3ʸ=35?
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Set u=2ˣ>0,v=3ʸ>0. Then u²+v²=74,uv=35.
steps: The listed pair corresponding to u=5,v=7 is(log₂5,log₃7).
problems.answer: (log₂5,log₃7); swapping u,v gives the other solution(log₂7,log₃5).

problems.title: Volume from three lateral-face areas
problems.question: A right triangular prism has base area4 and lateral-face areas9,10,17. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: If height is h,the base sides are9/h,10/h,17/h.
steps: The triangle with sides9,10,17 has semiperimeter18 and Heron area√(18·9·8·1)=36.

problems.title: Circumsphere of a cone frustum
problems.question: A cone frustum has radii8 and6,height14. Find its circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Put the lower radius8 base at z=0,upper radius6 base at z=14,and sphere center at z=t.

problems.title: Iterate an exponential function
problems.question: Given(1/3)^((1/3)ˣ)=x,find3^(−3^(−3^(−x))).
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Let f(t)=3^(−t). The hypothesis is f(f(x))=x.
steps: Apply f to both sides of the hypothesis to obtain f³(x)=f(x).

problems.title: Two equal irrational powers
problems.question: Evaluate12^√(log₁₂16)−16^√(log₁₆12).
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Take natural logs of each positive term.
steps: The second has exactly the same logarithm,so the two terms are equal.

problems.question: Find the cosine between cube lines A₁C and DC₁.
problems.idea: Use the identity or geometric relation below, including the domain restrictions.
formulas: Use direction vectors(1,1,−1) and(1,0,1).
steps: Their dot product is1−1=0,so the lines are perpendicular.
